A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SOMA, with matching authors, methods, and main experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally includes the supplement referenced by both versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original SKIM experiments comparing SOMA with LBS and HIT, quantitative architecture and regularization ablations, and qualitative deformation results in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds measured marker-visibility results and additional qualitative deformation examples in supplementary Sections 5–6.

M1.justification: The pose-driven muscle/skin decomposition, two U-Nets, canonical marker-residual supervision, regularizers, LBS, and barycentric muscle transfer remain unchanged. The supplement documents previously described components without establishing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the five-subject SKIM dataset for pose-driven skin and muscle deformation. V2 supplies demographics, acquisition routines, and more examples from that dataset; it does not establish an added dataset, population, or distinct evaluation task.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains LBS and HIT via SMPL as comparators. Tables 3–4 retain the same architecture and regularization variants. Supplementary baseline descriptions clarify these existing comparisons without adding evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 5 introduces a visibility-evaluation procedure aggregating coverage across frames and subjects, separating motions, and plotting per-frame elbow-flexor visibility during curls. No protocol revision is reported for the retained benchmarks; newly supplied training settings document existing experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds an analysis of marker coverage and pose-dependent occlusion, including elbow-flexor visibility histograms, plus a biceps case study at minimum and maximum flexion. The original architecture and loss ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experiments. The new visibility histograms describe variation across observed frames rather than uncertainty in estimated model performance.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their numerical results, including SOMA's 13.43 mm MPME. Supplementary Figure 3 adds coverage results, including 82.1% overall, 94.6% for triceps extensions, and 65.0% for push-ups. Supplementary Figures 4–5 add motion-specific and biceps deformation results.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 4 adds a focused derivation of signed prism volume using FEM shape functions, Jacobian integration, and polynomial-degree arguments establishing exact two-node Gauss–Legendre quadrature. V1 states this computation but does not contain the derivation; the existing regularizer is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty claim and three contributions: SKIM, SOMA's coupled deformation model, and propagation to individual muscles. The conclusion is lightly shortened without redefining the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges that force- and co-contraction-driven variation at a fixed joint angle remains unmodeled. Supplementary Section 5 also interprets reduced biceps/brachialis visibility at peak flexion as geometric occlusion while noting continued visibility of lateral bulging and the brachioradialis.

D1.justification: The supplement supplies extensive previously unavailable reproduction details: marker encoding and annotation, dataset organization, mesh specifications, trajectory refinement, network dimensions and activations, Adam training for 20 epochs with batch size 128 and learning rate 0.0001, loss weights, metric definitions, and muscle binding. The project URL and code/data availability claim are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including Dynamic FAUST, detailed moving-body capture, SFLsh, SoftSMPL, biharmonic weights, muscle incompressibility, and elasticity theory. These broaden supporting references without substantially changing the positioning against surface-only models, inverse anatomy methods, and simulations.

P1.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations through a structured supplement covering dataset construction, marker refinement, experimental setup, volume computation, visibility, qualitative examples, and muscle transfer. The main narrative remains largely intact, with limited conclusion/caption edits and an added acknowledgements section.

P2.justification: The supplement adds subject and annotation illustrations, visibility histograms, extensive deformation panels, and tables documenting demographics, meshes, motions, and dataset size. Existing main figures are retained but resized or reflowed, notably Figures 6–7; Figure 4 and ablation-table captions are refined.

improvement.justification: V1 defers essential reproduction details to a supplement absent from the supplied PDF. V2 supplies architecture, optimization, preprocessing, and volume-computation details, substantially improving reproducibility and scrutiny. Visibility evidence and the fixed-angle force limitation also improve transparency. Local documentation problems remain, including 2,310 markers versus the stated 1,000 IDs with two instances, but do not outweigh these substantial gains. The main benchmark evidence is unchanged.
